column1: # Process budget per path through the hooks (ww3d/playbook#734, decision 8), checked by cases/hook-budget.sh: what the
# path costs, measured on Windows 2026-11-26 in a checkout without open tick lists. Before a tool call `pb-hook
# pre-tool` starts bash only for a call a guard may act on, `pb-hook post-tool` after it starts no program (bar
# `uname` on an empty input); the other entries source their hook and read with the builtin (no second bash, no cat). The programs column is the full count of Linux: behind pb-hook the Git launcher
# puts /usr/bin before the shims, so Windows counts only the programs outside it (jq, gh) and holds the rest in the
# processes column. A hook that starts one program or process more turns the check red; lower the numbers with the
# path<TAB>programs at most (through shims; bash itself not counted)<TAB>processes at most (Windows job object over all
# entries of the path, the Git launcher and its console host included; Linux counts two a shell entry less, one an args entry)
